'''Clifford Michael Surko''' (October 11, 1941 – December 7, 2024<ref>{{cite web|url=https://adminrecords.ucsd.edu/Notices/2025/2025-3-20-2.html|title=In Memoriam: Clifford M. Surko, Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Physics and Professor of the Graduate Division|language=en|access-date=2025-03-22|publisher=adminrecords.ucsd.edu}}</ref>) was an American [[physicist]],<ref>{{Cite book|last=Gale Group.|title=American men & women of science.|date=2004|publisher=Gale|oclc=1082415302}}</ref> whose works involve [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]], [[atomic physics]], [[nonlinear dynamics]] and [[Solid-state physics|solid state physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sullivan|first1=J. P.|last2=Marler|first2=J. P.|last3=Gilbert|first3=S. J.|last4=Buckman|first4=S. J.|last5=Surko|first5=C. M.|date=2001|title=Excitation of Electronic States of Ar, ${H}_{2}$, and ${N}_{2}$ by Positron Impact|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=87|issue=7|article-number=073201|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.073201|pmid=11497889|hdl=1885/33430|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Surko|first1=C. M.|last2=Reif|first2=F.|date=1968|title=Investigation of a New Kind of Energetic Neutral Excitation in Superfluid Helium|journal=Physical Review|volume=175|issue=1|pages=229–241|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.175.229}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sullivan|first1=James P.|last2=Gilbert|first2=Steven J.|last3=Buckman|first3=Stephen J.|last4=Surko|first4=Clifford M.|date=2001|title=Search for resonances in the scattering of low-energy positrons from atoms and molecules|journal=Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics|language=en|volume=34|issue=15|pages=L467–L474|doi=10.1088/0953-4075/34/15/102|issn=0953-4075}}</ref> Together with his colleagues, he developed techniques for laser scattering at small angles to study waves and turbulence in [[tokamak]] plasmas and invented a positron trap (buffer gas positron trap) that was used in experiments worldwide to study [[antimatter]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Surko, Clifford M. Gianturco, Franco A., 1938-|title=New directions in antimatter chemistry and physics|date=2002|publisher=Kluwer Academic|oclc=839947424}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Surko|first=Clifford M.|date=2007|title=Atomic physics: A whiff of antimatter soup|url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?p=AONE&sw=w&issn=00280836&v=2.1&it=r&id=GALE%7CA185191467&sid=googleScholar&linkaccess=abs|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=449|issue=7159|pages=153–156|doi=10.1038/449153a|pmid=17851505|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Surko also developed other techniques for studying [[positron]] plasmas<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Surko|first1=C. M.|last2=Leventhal|first2=M.|last3=Passner|first3=A.|last4=Wysocki|first4=F. J.|date=1988|title=A positron plasma in the laboratory—how and why|journal=AIP Conference Proceedings|volume=175|issue=1|pages=75–90|doi=10.1063/1.37614|issn=0094-243X}}</ref> and examined atomic and plasma physics with positrons.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gribakin|first1=G. F.|last2=Young|first2=J. A.|last3=Surko|first3=C. M.|date=2010|title=Positron-molecule interactions: Resonant attachment, annihilation, and bound states|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=82|issue=3|pages=2557–2607|doi=10.1103/revmodphys.82.2557|issn=0034-6861|url=https://pure.qub.ac.uk/ws/files/742681/RevModPhys.82.2557.pdf}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Surko studied mathematics and physics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], with a [[bachelor's degree]] in 1964 and a [[doctorate]] in physics in 1968. He was a student of [[Frederick Reif]] at Berkeley.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lehrer |first=Erica |date=August 21, 2019 |title=Frederick Reif |url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/pt.6.4o.20190821a/full |access-date=June 17, 2022 |journal=Physics Today|doi=10.1063/pt.6.4o.20190821a |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was then at [[Bell Laboratories]] in Murray Hill, where he became department head for research in semiconductor and chemical physics in 1982. Since 1988, he has been a professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www-physics.ucsd.edu/fac_staff/fac_profile/faculty_description.php?person_id=231|title=UC San Diego {{!}} Faculty Profile|website=www-physics.ucsd.edu|access-date=2020-02-28}}</ref>

He was a visiting researcher at MIT (Plasma Fusion Center, 1977 to 1984), at [[École Polytechnique]] (1978/79) and at [[University College London]].

== Honors and awards ==
Surko was a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

In 2014, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''the invention of and development of techniques to accumulate, confine, and utilize [[positron]] plasmas, and for seminal experimental studies of waves and turbulence in [[tokamak]] plasmas''".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Surko&first_nm=Clifford&year=2014|title=2014 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-28}}</ref>
